**r = 0.0617** (Pearson correlation between gene length and mean expression for protein-coding genes in CD4 cells), with **n = 19,942** protein-coding genes, **p ≈ 2.77×10⁻¹⁸**.

Definition executed (approved): for each protein-coding gene, mean expression = arithmetic mean of the raw (batch-corrected) read counts across the **151 CD4 samples** (CD4 sets verified to match the expression columns 1:1); aligned by Geneid (row order identical across files); `scipy.stats.pearsonr(Length, mean_expr)` over **all 19,942** protein-coding genes, including the 1,518 zero-mean genes.

A very weak but statistically non-zero positive correlation: gene length explains essentially none of the variance in mean raw expression on this linear scale (r² ≈ 0.004). Note the r value is strongly dependent on the expression scale (see sensitivity table below).

**Sensitivity / alternative readings (for auditability):**

| Variant | n | r | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PRIMARY raw arithmetic mean (zeros incl.)** | 19,942 | **0.0617** | 2.77e-18 |
| Mean of log2(x+1) (zeros incl.) | 19,942 | 0.3155 | ≈0 |
| log2(mean raw), zero-mean excluded | 18,424 | 0.2568 | 3.5e-275 |
| Raw mean, zero-mean excluded | 18,424 | 0.0528 | 7.3e-13 |
| Spearman (raw mean) | 19,942 | 0.4394 | ≈0 |
| Mean of log2(CPM+1) | 19,942 | 0.3162 | ≈0 |

**Quality checks all clean:** GeneMetaInfo (59,453×5) – 0 missing; BatchCorrectedReadCounts (59,453×723) – 0 missing, all values integer-valued, non-negative, 57.9% zeros; Sample_annotated (723×6) – 0 missing; `Geneid` no duplicates, `Length` all numeric (range 8–347,964); meta index == expression row index == True; annotation CD4 set == CD4-labelled exp columns == True (151 = 151).

**Limitations:** the supplied matrix is integer and not size-normalized (column totals CV ≈ 0.44), so "mean expression" reflects the supplied scale; raw vs log2 changes r substantially (0.06 vs 0.32), which was flagged as an assumption, not a fact. Primary answer follows the raw-scale definition you authorised.
